chapters.headline: Scroll to Begin
chapters.title: Stanley Peninsula
chapters.description: The Stanley Peninsula is a picturesque coastal area on the southeastern tip of Hong Kong Island, known for its scenic waterfront, beaches, and historic landmarks. It combines natural beauty with vibrant local culture, making it one of Hong Kong's most popular seaside destinations.

chapters.headline: Sheer Scale and Heritage
chapters.title: Hong Kong's Largest Secondary School Campus
chapters.description: Spanning more than 40 acres, St. Stephen's College blends nearly a century of heritage architecture with contemporary educational facilities, creating one of Hong Kong's most distinctive learning environments.

chapters.headline: A Timeless Arrival
chapters.title: Main Entrance
chapters.description: The ceremonial gateway introduces visitors to nearly a century of architectural heritage and the enduring identity of St. Stephen's College.

chapters.headline: Hong Kong's Oldest Boarding School Landmark
chapters.title: School House
chapters.description: Completed in 1929 and inaugurated in 1930, the School House is the oldest surviving boarding-school building in Hong Kong and a declared monument. Its H-shaped design combines Western classical columns and arches with a Chinese-style roof suited to Hong Kong's climate. It now accommodates dormitories, classrooms, staff rooms, music rooms, and the College Library.

chapters.headline: A Century of Boarding Tradition
chapters.title: Martin Hostel
chapters.description: Built in 1929, Martin Hostel was later named in honour of Rev. Canon E. W. L. Martin, Principal and Warden from 1928 to 1953. This Grade II historic building retains much of its original timber flooring and blends European arches and granite columns with a Chinese-style roof. It continues to serve as a student hostel and includes dining, staff, and laundry facilities.

chapters.headline: A Place of Reflection
chapters.title: St. Stephen's Chapel
chapters.description: Opened in 1950 at the highest point of the campus, St. Stephen's Chapel is a Grade III historic building. It was built as a memorial to people who suffered and died during the Second World War and the Japanese occupation, including victims associated with the Stanley Internment Camp. The Chapel remains a place for worship, prayer, school services, and remembrance.

chapters.headline: Post-War Expansion
chapters.title: Classroom Block
chapters.description: The Classroom Block was built in 1964 to provide additional teaching space for the growing College. It reflects the post-war development of the campus and is listed as a Grade III historic building. It continues to house classrooms for daily teaching and learning.

chapters.headline: Knowledge and Discovery
chapters.title: Library
chapters.description: The College Library continues a long tradition of scholarship, providing a quiet centre for learning within the historic campus.

chapters.headline: Designed for Innovation
chapters.title: Special Room Block
chapters.description: The Special Room Block was opened in 1980 on the site of a former tennis court, replacing the old laboratory as the College expanded its specialist facilities. Designed by Dr. Tao Ho, its distinctive sloping walls and corridor layout earned a Hong Kong Institute of Architects Merit Award in 1982. The building now contains classrooms, science laboratories, computer rooms, and specialised teaching spaces.

chapters.headline: The Gathering Place
chapters.title: Ng Wah Hall
chapters.description: Ng Wah Hall was completed in 1970, during a period when St. Stephen's College was expanding after becoming co-educational. It provides a dedicated indoor venue for assemblies, performances, ceremonies, and other large school events. The hall is also listed as a Grade III historic building.

chapters.headline: Performance and Community
chapters.title: Tang Shiu Kin Hall
chapters.description: A vibrant venue where performances, celebrations, and student life come together, reflecting the College's strong sense of community.

chapters.headline: A New Chapter
chapters.title: Benevolence House
chapters.description: Benevolence House was inaugurated in 2022 as a major contemporary addition to the campus. Its design connects the historic school buildings with the sports field, while its sea-facing side contains classrooms and the Carol Yang Black Box Theatre. It now provides classrooms, a grand hall, an indoor fitness centre, student facilities, and an outdoor auditorium.

chapters.headline: Beyond the Classroom
chapters.title: Leung Kau Kui Student Centre
chapters.description: The Leung Kau Kui Student Centre was completed in 1988 to provide additional student-focused learning space. Its construction reflects the College's effort to broaden facilities beyond the original historic core of the campus. It is now used for classrooms and student activities.

chapters.headline: Life on Campus
chapters.title: North House and College House
chapters.description: From North House's post-war restoration to the modern College House, these residences continue St. Stephen's century-long boarding tradition.

chapters.headline: Preserving the Past
chapters.title: Heritage Gallery
chapters.description: Bungalow No. 3 was constructed in 1931 as staff quarters and has retained much of its original cottage-like character. After restoration supported by heritage funding, it was converted into the Heritage Gallery in 2011. The Grade II historic building now displays artefacts and stories about the College, the Battle of Hong Kong, and the Stanley Internment Camp.

chapters.headline: The Heart of Student Life
chapters.title: Central Square and Bell Plaza
chapters.description: Surrounded by historic architecture, these open spaces form the social heart of campus where students gather, celebrate, and connect every day.

chapters.headline: A Legacy of Sport
chapters.title: Tang Shiu Kin Sports Field
chapters.description: The Tang Shiu Kin Sports Field began as a swamp that was filled in during the 1920s to reduce the risk of malaria. During the Japanese occupation, it became a vegetable garden connected with the Stanley Internment Camp, and it was renamed after Sir Tang Shiu Kin funded its re-turfing in 1975. Following later refurbishments, it now provides a football pitch, athletics facilities, and space for physical education.

chapters.headline: One Campus. One Legacy.
chapters.title: St. Stephen's College
chapters.description: For over a century, St. Stephen's College has united heritage, innovation, and the beauty of Stanley Peninsula into one of Hong Kong's most remarkable educational campuses.
